sources_and_data: Direct symbolic proof from the finite-tree matching-swap definitions
Irving and Rattan, Minimal Factorizations of Permutations into Star Transpositions, arXiv:math/0610640, Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2
Pak, Reduced decompositions of permutations in terms of star transpositions, Discrete Mathematics 204 (1999)
method: Define a token-labelled branch-flow multigraph and a schedule-specific occupancy dependency graph; audit the fixed-center star formula against primary star-factorization literature; then construct and hand-verify an overlapping adjacent-hub family with a forced four-round schedule.
uncertainty: The exact H_h obstruction is finite and does not establish an asymptotic approximation gap.
The high-degree parameter is carried by fixed inert leaves, so active high-load hub growth remains untested.
A refined schedule-independent precedence-chain certificate and a constructive exchange-ordering theorem remain open.
mathematical_claim: The fixed-center star formula m'+q is known star-transposition factorization prior art. For the high-degree double-hub family H_h obtained from a-u-v-b by adding fixed leaves at u and v, with A<->B and U<->V, OPT(H_h,d)=4 while LB_hub(H_h,d)=3. The naive flow-cycle certificate max_v(W(v)+c_v), where c_v counts labelled branch-flow cycles, is therefore unsound: it predicts at least 5 on this family.
assumptions: T is a finite undirected tree with one token initially at each vertex and a bijective destination map.
A parallel round is a matching and swaps the endpoint tokens on every selected edge.
H_h has active path a-u-v-b and h-2 fixed pendant leaves at each hub for every integer h>=2.
The active target sends A at a to b, B at b to a, U at u to v, and V at v to u; all added leaf tokens are fixed.
The candidate cycle certificate charges one extra incident swap for each directed cycle of the token-labelled branch-flow multigraph after deleting zero-flow inert branches.
verified_steps: Irving-Rattan's primary theorem gives minimal transitive star-factorization length n+m-2, and its fixed-point corollary yields m'+q for the fixed-center star; Pak is the earlier restricted fixed-pivot result.
For every vertex v, source and destination branch maps define a labelled balanced directed multigraph F_v; token labels are retained and branch multiplicity is not collapsed.
The schedule-specific dependency graph P(sigma) records same-token order, same-vertex capacity order, and actual occupancy order, showing why F_v alone cannot determine all scheduling dependencies.
For H_h, r(au)=1, r(uv)=2, r(vb)=1, D=3, W(u)=W(v)=3, and no fixed-hub term applies, so LB_hub=3.
The four matching rounds {au,vb}, {uv}, {au,vb}, {uv} reach the target while leaving inert leaves fixed.

In any hypothetical three-round schedule, A and B must move every round along their unique length-three paths, forcing exactly the first three matching patterns; the resulting state has U and V unswapped, so round four is necessary.
At each active hub, F_v is the disjoint union of two directed 2-cycles, so the candidate W(v)+c_v lower bound would be 5 and is contradicted by the exact four-round schedule.
gaps: No schedule-independent refined dependency certificate beyond the falsified naive cycle count was proved.
No universal constant-factor upper bound relative to LB_hub was proved.
No unbounded separation between OPT and LB_hub was established.
No polynomial token-preserving exchange-ordering algorithm was established.
The high-degree parameter h is carried by fixed inert leaves; the result does not prove a growing high-load obstruction at active hubs.

parameters.fixed_inert_leaves: h-2 at each of u and v

checks: The star formula was independently mapped to the primary Irving-Rattan length theorem and Pak's earlier restricted result.
The H_h lower bound uses only unique-path distance forcing, not computation or an unverified schedule assertion.
The four-round upper schedule was written round by round and every round is a matching.
The branch-flow cycle count was evaluated with token labels and the inert high-degree branches were explicitly separated.
The finite obstruction was not promoted to an unbounded lower bound or an approximation theorem.
independent_review.scope_limit: The counterexample closes only the stated naive cycle-count certificate. It does not resolve the general LB_hub stretch conjecture or every possible dependency-aware certificate.

fully_proved: The candidate max_v(W(v)+c_v) is false on H_h
The token-labelled branch-flow and schedule-specific dependency objects are well-defined
independently_reproduced: The exact H_h value follows both from the explicit four-round schedule and the forced three-round contradiction
known_prior_art: Fixed-center multi-cycle star formula as a star-transposition factorization length
Pak's restricted fixed-pivot star factorization result
finite_counterexample_only: The H_h family is a constant-size active obstruction embedded at arbitrary degree; it is not an asymptotic approximation lower bound
plausible_but_unproved: A refined dependency certificate based on schedule-independent precedence chains
A constant-factor schedule relative to LB_hub
disproved: One extra incident swap per labelled branch-flow cycle is a valid arbitrary-tree lower bound

next_falsifiable_action: Without executing an experiment, prove or refute a schedule-independent precedence-chain certificate that strictly refines LB_hub on overlapping active hubs; if no such certificate survives, close branch-flow cycle counting and move to a different tree-scheduling invariant.
observed_result_or_blocker: A complete bounded mathematical increment was obtained: the star novelty claim was corrected, a token-labelled dependency formalism was fixed, and the naive flow-cycle lower bound was disproved by an exact adjacent-hub family. The general LB_hub approximation question remains open.
